reading.body:
DataPro USA Web Development is not a data center: its domain is a parked for-sale page, its address resolves to a different occupant, and it publishes no capacity.

The record carries a data center tag from OpenStreetMap, zero megawatts, no operator, and no published specifications. Reverse geocoding the stored coordinates returns Hole Hunter Industries at 7741 East Gray Road in Scottsdale, a different current occupant. The coordinates sit several miles from the other eight rows in the same batch, so no single shared building connects them. The company's own domain, dataprousa.com, is a parked GoDaddy for-sale page, consistent with an inactive or defunct small web development business.

Any inventory of AI-relevant data center capacity assembled from public registries inherits errors like this one. A record with zero megawatts, no operator, and no specifications contributes nothing to compute supply, and counting it as a facility inflates the total. The correct treatment here is subtraction, not addition.

What the data does not say is how many other entries carry the same mistag, whether this business ever operated servers, or what power and connectivity the address had. It covers one point at one address, and the batch of eight other rows is referenced only as a distance check. No conclusion about the wider Arizona facility count follows from it.
